transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-22 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 min
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (CTO - Cascade), Maya (ML Eng), Samir (SRE), Olga (Product)

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, welcome, thanks for joining. we wanted to focus today on the latency/throughput SLOs for the POC and make sure the measurement plan lines up with your production traffic.
00:18 Evan: Great thanks Jordan. real quick context — we plan to run a three week POC, then a 30 day pilot if results look good. main use is chat-based summarization and routing, 60% of requests are short prompts (~50 tokens), 40% are long (~450 tokens).
00:35 Jordan: Perfect — that mix matters a lot for TTFT and TPOT. Priya will walk through our suggested benchmarks and metrics.
00:46 Priya: Hi all. quick definitional check: when we say TTFT we mean time-to-first-token, that's the tail latency that impacts interactive feel — relevant for chat. TPOT is time-per-output-token (sometimes 'per-token' throughput) which matters for cost and sustained throughput. vendors sometimes measure differently so we'll be explicit in the plan.
01:10 Maya: can you give an example target we'd expect? we want to compare hosted versus dedicated.
01:18 Priya: Sure. as a baseline for interactive chat we'd propose p95 TTFT < 180 ms, p99 < 350 ms for short prompts (50 tokens). for longer requests we look at p95 TTFT < 350 ms, p99 < 600 ms. TPOT we measure in ms/token during steady stream — target p95 TPOT < 40 ms/token on dedicated GPUs with batching for the long requests, hosted will be slightly higher. these are starting points — we can tune quantization, batch sizes, and routing.
01:58 Samir: those numbers look ok, but our regulatory constraints mean we'll likely use a private deployment behind a VPC with KMS. network egress will add jitter. we need to measure under realistic network conditions.
02:12 Priya: absolutely — part of the measurement plan is to run benchmarks from your VPC (private) and from a hosted baseline so we can compare delta. we'll also simulate your egress and latency distribution.
02:26 Olga: what's the difference again practically between TTFT and TPOT — which should we optimize for?
02:32 Priya: Good question. TTFT is perceived latency — the time the user sees the first token and decides system is responsive. TPOT is throughput efficiency and affects per-token cost and sustained latency under load. For chat UX we prioritize TTFT; for batch generation or long-form we obsess on TPOT so cost doesn't explode. In practice we set dual SLOs: TTFT p95/p99 targets for interactive flows and TPOT p95 targets for long-running generation.
03:05 Evan: ok that dual approach makes sense. what's your measurement methodology?
03:10 Priya: We do controlled benchmarks with your sample prompts and traffic mix at different concurrencies. Steps: 1) baseline single-request cold run to capture cold-start/compilation overhead; 2) steady-state runs at target concurrency (e.g., 50 qps, 100 qps) to measure TPOT and throughput; 3) tail-latency stress tests with spikes and jitter to capture p95/p99. We capture both client-side timings and server-side timings (TTFT server vs total including network). We prefer collecting both so we can separate network jitter from inference time.
03:52 Maya: can you do the runs with our prompt set? we have a mix of classification + summarization + few-shot prompts.
03:59 Priya: yes please send the 1k representative prompts. ideally include the tokenized lengths distribution. we'll run the benchmark across your model variants — e.g., base open model and a quantized variant — and on dedicated pool and hosted.
04:18 Jordan: timeline wise we propose: Jordan sends pricing and perf spreadsheet today, Priya runs an initial baseline within 5 business days, then a pilot kickoff 1 week after baseline. that aligns with the three week POC pilot.
04:33 Samir: we need to confirm we can open the required IP ranges for dedicated nodes, and our security team will request SOC2 docs.
04:40 Jordan: yes we'll share SOC2 + security pack. that will be in the next steps.
04:46 Priya: on metrics to report — we'll provide p50/p90/p95/p99 for TTFT and p50/p95 for TPOT, average tokens per request, end-to-end latency, server-side inference time, and throughput (max QPS sustained at SLO).
05:10 Maya: for TPOT are you measuring ms per token including tokenization overhead?
05:15 Priya: we can provide both: inference-only ms/token and end-to-end ms/token including tokenization and network to help you compute cost estimates.
05:25 Evan: what about batching — does batching harm TTFT?
05:28 Priya: there's a tradeoff. batching increases throughput and lowers cost per token but can add a small TTFT delay for the first token if we wait to fill a batch. Redwood's runtime supports adaptive batching where we put strict upper bounds to keep TTFT within target. we'll also test quantized models which reduce per-token time.
05:52 Samir: are you planning to test tail behavior like p99 under traffic spikes and cold cache?
05:56 Priya: Yes — we'll include stress tests with sudden 3x spikes and empty KV cache scenarios, plus tests after model load/unload to measure cold compiles. We'll capture TTFT increase during cold starts.
06:10 Olga: success criteria — what are you proposing to call the POC a success?
06:15 Jordan: Proposed success criteria in plain terms: 1) under customer's representative traffic mix, TTFT p95/p99 meet the agreed targets for interactive flows, 2) TPOT p95 within threshold for long-form generation at target cost-per-1k tokens, 3) no critical security blockers for private deployment, 4) runbook for autoscaling and fallbacks validated. If all met we move to pilot/commit.
06:42 Evan: acceptable. we'll sign off on the exact numbers in the perf spreadsheet after we see baseline results.
06:48 Priya: ok i'll outline the concrete targets we discussed: for short chat (50 tokens) TTFT p95 150-180ms, p99 300-400ms; long requests (450 tokens) TTFT p95 300-450ms, p99 600-900ms; TPOT p95 <= 50ms/token on dedicated, <= 70ms/token hosted. We'll label these provisional.
07:18 Maya: curious about instrumentation — what traces and logs do you provide?
07:22 Priya: we provide per-request traces, token timing breakdown, KV cache hit rates, batching stats, kernel selection logs, and per-route dashboards. we can export logs to your splunk or datadog.
07:36 Samir: KMS integration detail? we use AWS KMS — need to know HSM vs managed keys path.
07:41 Jordan: we'll include the KMS integration docs in the security pack.
07:45 Evan: for measurement plan, what exactly will you deliver at the end of baseline run? a CSV with latencies and a slide deck?
07:52 Priya: deliverables: 1) raw CSV/ndjson of request-level metrics, 2) summarized PDF with p50/p90/p95/p99 and TPOT charts, 3) config used (batch sizes, quantization), 4) recommended tuning steps and estimated cost per 1k tokens.
08:12 Olga: do we need a dedicated cluster for the POC or can hosted suffice?
08:16 Jordan: initial baseline can be hosted but given regulatory concerns we'll run the main POC in your private VPC (private offering). we can do a hybrid: hosted for feature parity and private for compliance and final benchmarks.
08:30 Maya: bandwidth — our peak qps estimate is 120 QPS with 3 second SLA for user interactions. how do we size?
08:36 Priya: for 120 QPS with your token mix, rough sizing: for short requests mostly CPU light but for long-form you'll want ~4-8 GPUs depending on model and quantization. we'll produce a more precise capacity plan after the baseline.
08:52 Samir: can you include cost vs latency tradeoff curves?
08:55 Priya: yes we'll include curves showing latency vs cost per 1k tokens across quantization and batch size configs.
09:05 Evan: timeline recap?
09:07 Jordan: Jordan to send perf/pricing sheet today; Priya runs baseline within 5 business days after getting prompts; bench results and tuning in the following week; pilot kickoff targeted 2027-06-29; POC finishes ~3 weeks after kickoff.
09:28 Maya: ok thanks, we will send prompts and traces by tomorrow.
09:33 Priya: quick note on measurement specifics: when measuring p99 we prefer at least 100k requests or synthetic mixtures with bootstrapped confidence intervals so p99 is meaningful. we'll call out sample sizes in the baseline report.
09:51 Samir: one more operational question: how do you handle routing fallback during capacity pressure?
09:55 Jordan: Redwood supports policy-based routing and automatic fallback to smaller model variants or region-level fallback. we'll include a runbook and explanation of how graceful degradation looks.
10:08 Evan: cool. thanks everyone. we'll watch for Jordan's email and Priya's benchmark plan.
10:14 Jordan: thanks all, talk soon. recap and next steps in the calendar invite.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings, e.g., 'TTFT' read correctly but sometimes auto-transcript shows 'T-T-F-T', product names maybe lowercased. some timestamps approximate.
